# Goal

AI implements the project quickly. Alex learns from implementation plans, pull requests, code review, and questions.

The workflow must prevent large unexplained changes and must avoid horizontal “backend first, mobile later” epics.

## Source check

Before planning an issue:

1. Read the five canonical documents.
2. Read the active milestone and issue.
3. Inspect the relevant repository code and tests.
4. Ignore every document marked ARCHIVED.
5. Ask Alex when a product choice is not settled.

Do not infer current requirements from the Decision Log or an archived design.

Use only Approved artifacts from [MVP Visual Design and Approved Screens](<https://linear.app/hintology/document/canonical-mvp-visual-design-and-approved-screens-7b137621de9b>). A screenshot controls presentation, not behavior.

## Vertical slices

Default to a vertical slice. A slice delivers a small capability a person can use through every required layer.

A slice may touch:

* Django model or migration;
* service and serializer;
* endpoint and schema;
* generated API client;
* React Native screen or component;
* tests;
* deployed configuration.

End every issue description with: `A user can now ...`

A ticket that ends with only “the model exists” or “the endpoint exists” is horizontal. Use a horizontal ticket only when it is an enabling safety control, a migration prerequisite, or work with no honest user-facing endpoint. State the reason in the issue.

## Slice order

Use this order inside a new capability:

1. Smallest complete happy path.
2. Common correction and editing.
3. Failure and empty states.
4. Cost, quota, and operational controls.
5. Polish after behavior is stable.

Use manual before AI when manual proves the domain model. Use deterministic behavior before AI when both solve the same problem.

## Issue size

One focused Linear issue normally maps to one pull request.

An issue includes:

* user outcome;
* scope;
* out of scope;
* acceptance criteria;
* affected layers;
* test expectations;
* dependencies;
* manual acceptance steps;
* the final `A user can now ...` sentence.

Avoid tiny issues that exist only to satisfy process. Avoid an issue so large that its PR cannot be reviewed in one sitting.

## Implementation plan

Before code, AI writes a concise implementation plan that covers:

* current behavior;
* files and layers affected;
* chosen approach;
* important alternatives rejected;
* React Native or Django concepts involved;
* migration and API-contract effects;
* tests;
* risks and open questions.

Alex approves the plan before implementation. The approved plan is saved with the ticket work.

## Pull request

Each PR:

* uses the Linear issue in the title;
* explains the user outcome first;
* lists meaningful architecture choices;
* calls out migrations and generated-client changes;
* names the most important files for Alex to review;
* reports automated and manual verification;
* states known follow-ups;
* does not merge itself.

### UI screenshots

Every pull request that changes user-visible UI includes screenshots before review.

* Show each new primary screen or the states changed by the PR.
* Include before and after images when an existing screen changes materially.
* Include relevant empty, loading, error, or destructive states when the PR changes them.
* Use a live simulator, device, or web render. A design mockup may be labeled as a design reference, but it is not proof of the implementation.
* Upload review-only screenshots to the GitHub PR description or a PR comment. Do not commit screenshots solely for PR review.
* If an existing tracked image is reused, embed its existing URL instead of adding a duplicate.
* A non-UI PR states that screenshots are not applicable.

Alex decides when to merge.

## Learning

Do not turn every PR description into a tutorial. Explain the decisions that matter. When Alex asks why, explain the reusable concept, the pattern name, its tradeoffs, and when another approach would be better.

## Design

Use the canonical MVP experience and current visual system during implementation. Do not redesign opportunistically.

Design-quality tooling such as Impeccable belongs in a named follow-up or a deliberate polish issue. It must preserve the established visual direction unless Alex approves a redesign.

## Done

A slice is done when:

* acceptance criteria pass;
* relevant tests pass;
* the API client is regenerated when needed;
* the behavior works on the intended device path;
* the PR explains the change;
* documentation no longer claims behavior that the slice reversed.
